more.good_when: A maintainer who runs the tests finds no runner of overnight still going on the machine once they end. Now each run of the tests leaves one behind for hours, from test_a_work_added_while_another_runs_waits_in_the_queue_after_it: the blog's add starts a second runner, which takes the queue once the case stops the first, retries the shop's work against a double with no run left (its log shows `IndexError: list index out of range. Retry 2 of 7`), and waits through all 7 retries. After 8 runs of the tests, `pgrep -af scripts/runner` showed 8 such runners.

A maintainer who changes how `queue.run` looks for the pending works, with its behavior kept, sees every queue test still pass. Now test_a_work_added_just_as_the_runner_ends_still_runs replaces `queue.pending` inside the module by monkeypatch, so the case holds only while `run` calls it by that module name. A change to that call fails the case at `added[0]`, though a work added as the runner ends still runs.

A fault in how the runner carries the works in order fails one test, which names that case. Now test_the_runner_carries_the_works_one_after_another_in_the_order_they_were_added, with two works, and test_the_runner_carries_ten_works_each_once_in_the_order_they_were_added, with ten, run the same branches of `queue.run` for the same case and fail together.
